messages: maria: Quick design check — I'm trying a 'ghost lineage' visual in the rollout timeline to show branch vs linear versions. Figma preview: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/rollout-timeline#node-id=123 — can you eyeball clarity + a11y implications? owen: Looks good visually. My concern: users might interpret the ghost line as an active merge rather than a fork. Can we add a small label like 'forked from v3.1' on hover or focus? maria: Yeah hover labels are planned, but hover alone isn't accessible. Sam, thoughts on SR/keyboard? sam: Screen reader note — if the ghost line is conveying topology (fork vs linear) it can't be purely decorative. We need a textual equivalent. Suggest making each timeline node keyboard-focusable and providing an accessible description such as 'v3.2, forked from v3.1, 20% traffic'. Also consider an ARIA role (e.g., list + listitem or region) so assistive tech can parse the group. :eyes: devin: Implementation sketch: nodes as buttons with aria-describedby pointing to an sr-only description. Quick example: ```html Forked from v3.1, 20% traffic ``` This keeps DOM lightweight and lets us announce details on focus. chloe: Perf caveat — some enterprise customers can have O(100) versions in history (we've seen ~200). I worry about rendering 200 sr-only description nodes upfront. Can we lazy-render descriptions only for nodes in viewport or a11y-focus? sam: Good call. Recommendation: collapsed summary for the timeline (e.g., '20 versions — use arrow keys to navigate') and only render per-node descriptions when a node receives focus or when the timeline is expanded. Also use an aria-live polite region to announce expansion state changes so screenreader users aren't lost. maria: Visual note — ghost line opacity currently at 35% on the mock. Contrast-wise it's decorative, but since it conveys relationships, we should ensure the line weight/contrast communicates clearly without relying solely on color. Maybe increase thickness or add subtle dotted pattern for forks vs linear. owen: UX nit: keyboard order must follow visual left-to-right. For wrapped or stacked layouts we should still ensure logical DOM order so Tab navigation feels consistent. devin: I'll prototype the keyboard interactions: left/right arrow to move focus between nodes, Enter/Space to open details, and a single live region to announce 'v3.2 focused — forked from v3.1, 20% traffic'. Will also explore lazy rendering of sr-only spans. chloe: I'll run a perf check on rendering 200 nodes with lazy vs eager sr-only DOM elements. If we need to virtualize the list, let's coordinate early because it affects animation timing. sam: Once devin has a prototype, I'll run it through VoiceOver + NVDA and check keyboard-only flows. Also check that the live region announcements aren't too noisy when quickly arrowing through nodes. maria: Action items: devin -> build prototype; sam -> a11y sign-off; chloe -> perf validation. Let's sync tomorrow 11:00am PT. Thanks all :thumbsup:
